blocks.text: [II, 714] And in Damir: لحمه عسر الهضم ردي المزاج وهي يولد كيموسا غليظا [laḥmuhu ʿasir al-haḍm radī al-mizāj wa-hiya yuwallid kaymūsan ghalīẓan], Its flesh is difficult to digest, of a bad temperament, and it produces a thick chyme. In Avicenna: لحوم الطواويس صلبة [luḥūm al-ṭawāwīs ṣulba], The flesh of peacocks is hard. In Mesue: ردي المزاج [radī al-mizāj], of bad juice; whence Juvenal in his first Satire:
— — you carry the undigested peacock into the baths: hence sudden deaths, and an old age without a will.

Therefore, apart from that exceptional beauty, there was no reason why the peacock was so highly valued among the ancients. Indeed, the Arabs imagine that the peacock, however beautiful, is nonetheless a bird of ill omen, because, as they tell the tale, كان سببا لدخول ابليس الجنة وخروج ادم منها [kāna sababan li-dukhūl Iblīs al-janna wa-khurūj Ādam minhā], it was the reason why the devil entered Paradise, and why Adam went out of it. But for what reason, I have not yet found. Of the same sort is what the anonymous author of the روضة العلما [Rawḍat al-ʿulamā], Garden [col. 140] of the Learned, reports: that the vine was sprinkled by the devil with the blood of four animals, namely of the peacock when it was first planted, of the ape when it began to put out leaves, of the lion when it pushed out its grapes, and finally of the pig when the fruit was already ripening. And that this is why whoever drinks wine 1. becomes more handsome, like the peacock; 2. plays, dances and gesticulates in the manner of an ape; 3. rages like a lion; 4. like a pig

God's words in Iob. XXXIX, 13., כנף רננים נעלסה, are explained by most of the more recent writers, following Kimchi and Pomarius, as The wing of the peacocks exults, as though it dealt with peacocks, which take pride in the beauty of their feathers. Yet in that passage רננים are ostriches, not peacocks, as we prove at length in the treatise On the Ostrich; and those who interpret them as peacocks rest on no reasoning, although today no explanation of this word is more widely accepted.
